Orthophosphoric acid (H₃PO₄) is **polar**. Its phosphorus center has an approximately **tetrahedral** arrangement of four oxygen atoms. The structure has one P=O bond and three P–OH bonds, as reflected in the retrieved SMILES `O=P(O)(O)O`; because these bonds are not all equivalent, their dipoles do **not** cancel, leaving a net molecular dipole.

The molecular profile confirms the formula H₃O₄P and this connectivity. It did not report a numerical dipole moment or a measured geometry.
